execution.scqa_summary:
Situation: Year-to-date gross margin percentage is underperforming against target when compared to the same period last year.

Complication: Five product lines are driving the shortfall, with Synthetic Blend Engine Oil declining 7.1 percentage points, Conventional Engine Oil down 6.6 points, and Compressor Oil down 5.9 points; the Value product category has also contracted 6.4 percentage points, and no segments are performing at or above healthy levels.

Question: What is causing margin compression across our core oil products and value-tier offerings, and which of these declines represents the greatest financial exposure?

Answer: The data indicates systematic margin pressure in our engine oil portfolio and value segment, with Synthetic Blend Engine Oil representing the largest single deterioration at 7.1 points; immediate investigation should focus on pricing power, product mix shift toward lower-margin SKUs, and cost inflation in these five segments to quantify total margin impact and identify recovery levers.

what_is.text: Issue observed during year_to_date compared against prior year_to_date.
Largest variance in product_name: Synthetic Blend Engine Oil (Δ -7.14).
Analysis scoped by applied filters, limiting impact to selected context.

where_is.text: customer_name: National Auto Parts Chain A (Δ -5.24)

market_conflict.summary: All four external signals—base oil supply tightness, crude volatility, EV-driven demand softness, and private-label price competition—are consistent headwinds that corroborate the internal margin compression finding, with no contradictory tailwinds identified.

options_ranked.title: Non-Locked Repricing Plus Post-Lock Premium Mix Acceleration (Structural Mix Correction)
options_ranked.description: Reprice non-anchor/spot-market sales of Synthetic Blend and Conventional Engine Oil in the near term, then launch a post-quarter promotional campaign to shift customer mix toward High Mileage and full synthetic formulations, which retain a relative margin premium (Synthetic Blend at 20.64% vs. Conventional at 19.16% in the current period) despite both having declined. Scoped to the same non-anchor Engine Oils and Value-tier segments as opt_1; other product lines and regions performing within threshold remain out of scope. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: Synthetic Blend Engine Oil is itself the single worst-performing segment by absolute decline (-7.14pts) in this dataset, so pushing volume toward it before its own margin stabilizes risks amplifying exposure to the same cost pressure. Resolution path: Step 1 is to confirm Synthetic Blend margin has stabilized (via the opt_1 surcharge and base-oil lag clearing) for at least one reporting cycle; Step 2 is to then accelerate the mix-shift campaign once the underlying segment margin is no longer actively eroding.
options_ranked.rationale: Combines an immediate repricing lever with a structural root-cause fix (premium mix rebalancing) that leverages the still-intact relative margin premium of synthetic formulations, addressing both the timing mismatch and the underlying mix vulnerability BCG identified.

arguments_for: Captures near-term repricing recovery while building a structural, multi-period margin uplift via mix shift toward higher-margin formulations.
Synthetic Blend retains a 1.48pt margin premium over Conventional in the current period, so the mix thesis is directionally supported by present data.
arguments_against: The premium_mix_pct -> gross_margin_pct relationship this option depends on is an unconfirmed industry-template assumption, not a client-validated relationship.
Promoting volume into Synthetic Blend before its own margin stabilizes could concentrate more exposure in the worst-performing segment.
key_questions: Has Synthetic Blend margin stabilized before committing promotional spend to accelerate its mix share?
What promotional discount rate is required to shift mix, and does it erode more margin than the mix benefit recovers?

arguments_for: Sales and marketing teams can execute repricing and promotional design using existing account infrastructure without new systems.
arguments_against: Running two sequential campaigns (repricing then mix-shift) within one planning cycle strains commercial team bandwidth.
key_questions: What is the realistic lead time to design and launch a post-lock promotional campaign without diverting resources from opt_1 execution?

implementation_triggers: Anchor contract lock expiry dates approaching for a material share of volume
Confirmation that Synthetic Blend margin has stabilized (see unresolved tension)
Repricing of non-locked sales executed and tracked for one full cycle
prerequisites: Confirmed non-locked account list (shared with opt_1)
Marketing/sales capacity to design and launch a post-lock promotional campaign
Validated premium_mix_pct trend data to confirm the mix-shift thesis before spend

impact_estimate.basis: Sized from the Synthetic Blend Engine Oil -7.14pt change point: repricing ~50% of non-locked volume recovers 40-65% of that segment decline (2.8-4.6pt), with an additional 1-2pt sought from mix-shift in subsequent periods. This is a segment-level (Engine Oils) estimate; it is NOT a direct restatement of the smaller -4.49pt enterprise-wide decline, and its high end approaches nearly the full enterprise-wide move despite being sized from one product's decline.
impact_estimate.scope_label: Non-anchor Synthetic Blend & Conventional Engine Oil sales plus premium-mix shift

key_assumptions.assumption: Premium mix (Synthetic/High Mileage) still carries a structural margin premium over Conventional despite recent compression.
key_assumptions.provenance: Consistent with current-period change point values (Synthetic Blend 20.64% vs. Conventional 19.16%); confirm premium persists in the next reporting period.

key_assumptions.assumption: Repricing of non-locked/spot sales can be executed within the current quarter before base-oil costs plateau.
key_assumptions.provenance: Base oil spot price index trend over the next 4-6 weeks.

key_assumptions.assumption: The premium_mix_pct -> gross_margin_pct relationship will hold, so a mix-shift promotional campaign will structurally lift blended margin.
key_assumptions.provenance: Template/unconfirmed industry prior; track blended margin change in periods where premium_mix_pct increases post-campaign.

flagged_side_effects: Promotional mix-shift spend could compress margin further in the short term if incentives are priced too aggressively before Synthetic Blend margin stabilizes.

options_ranked.title: Non-Anchor Surcharge & Value-Tier Dynamic Pricing (Immediate Cost Pass-Through)
options_ranked.description: Implement a temporary raw-material surcharge (0.5-1.0% of invoice value) on non-anchor, spot/transactional lubricant sales and on Value-tier products (currently 19.82% margin, down 6.42pts), effective within 30 days. This is scoped explicitly to Synthetic Blend Engine Oil, Conventional Engine Oil, and Value-tier SKUs sold outside contractually locked anchor accounts — the anchor book itself (price-locked mid-quarter per the known constraint) is out of scope and untouched. Segments not named in the top change points (other product lines, customer regions performing within threshold) are also out of scope for this action; no broad price action is proposed there.
options_ranked.rationale: Directly and quickly offsets the confirmed base_oil_cost->cogs pass-through lag without violating the anchor price-lock clause, using the highest-margin-deterioration segments (Synthetic Blend, Value tier) as the sizing basis.

arguments_for: Recovers margin from the exact non-locked channels where the base-oil cost pass-through is currently uncompensated by price.
Requires no new capital investment and can be reversed instantly if base oil prices normalize.
arguments_against: The 40-50% addressable-volume assumption underlying the recovery range is not confirmed by an actual account-level revenue split.
A surcharge alone does not address the root cause if base oil costs continue rising beyond the current lag window.
key_questions: What percentage of Synthetic Blend, Conventional, and Value-tier revenue is genuinely outside the anchor price lock?
How will the surcharge be communicated to avoid it reading as an opportunistic price hike?

arguments_for: Preserves the negotiated relationship and pricing certainty for anchor accounts, protecting the highest-value contractual relationships.
arguments_against: Non-anchor, price-sensitive spot/transactional customers may be the most surcharge-sensitive segment, risking volume loss precisely where margin recovery is targeted.
key_questions: What is the price elasticity of non-anchor lubricant buyers, and has this been tested in any prior surcharge event?

implementation_triggers: Confirmed non-anchor account list from Sales/Contracts
Base oil spot price index remaining elevated relative to its 6-month average
CFO budget/pricing-policy approval
prerequisites: Legal/contracts confirmation of which accounts fall outside the anchor price-lock clause
Pricing systems capability to apply a differentiated surcharge line-item by account type
Finance sign-off on surcharge rate and duration

impact_estimate.basis: Sized from the Synthetic Blend Engine Oil (-7.14pt) and Value-tier (-6.42pt) segment change points: a 0.5-1.0% surcharge applied to an estimated 40-50% addressable non-anchor volume recovers 2.1-3.8 of the 7.14pt segment decline. This is a segment-level estimate (Engine Oils + Value tier), not a direct restatement of the -4.49pt enterprise-wide decline.
impact_estimate.scope_label: Non-anchor Synthetic Blend, Conventional Engine Oil & Value-tier sales

key_assumptions.assumption: Non-anchor/spot and Value-tier channels represent 40-50% of total addressable Synthetic Blend + Conventional Engine Oil + Value-tier volume.
key_assumptions.provenance: Sales revenue split report showing anchor vs. non-anchor account share for these SKUs.

key_assumptions.assumption: Base oil cost pass-through lag is approximately 1 month, so current-period margin compression reflects a spot-price spike from 1-2 periods prior.
key_assumptions.provenance: Confirmed by client per causal register: base_oil_cost -> cogs mechanism, ~1 month lag, confirmed provenance.

key_assumptions.assumption: Non-anchor customers will tolerate a 0.5-1.0% surcharge without material volume loss.
key_assumptions.provenance: Volume/order trend for surcharged accounts over the first 60 days post-implementation.

flagged_side_effects: Non-anchor customers may perceive the surcharge as opportunistic pricing, risking relationship strain in competitive channels.

options_ranked.title: SKU-Level Price Realization Plus Q3-Q4 Base-Oil Forward Contracting (Structural Procurement Hedge)
options_ranked.description: Execute targeted 3-5% price increases on non-anchor Synthetic Blend and Conventional Engine Oil SKUs within 30 days, and simultaneously engage procurement to lock in base-oil forward contracts for Q3-Q4 delivery at current spot levels. Scoped to the same non-anchor segments within Engine Oils as opt_1/opt_2; anchor accounts remain untouched, and product lines/regions performing within threshold are excluded. This option extends beyond the 90-day window into a longer procurement commitment and is therefore the least reversible of the three.
options_ranked.rationale: Pairs immediate price realization with a forward-looking procurement hedge that removes future base-oil volatility from the margin equation, giving the most durable protection against a repeat of this lag-driven compression, at the cost of locking in capital commitments.

arguments_for: Forward contracting directly removes the confirmed base_oil_cost volatility mechanism from future COGS, addressing the root cause rather than just its symptom.
Combines a near-term price lever with a structural hedge, offering the broadest recovery range of the three options.
arguments_against: Locking forward contracts at current spot levels creates an opportunity-cost risk if base oil prices subsequently fall.
Two-thirds of the claimed recovery range depends on preventing future erosion, not reversing the already-realized 7.14pt decline, which may overstate near-term impact.
key_questions: What is the cost and contractual flexibility of available base-oil forward contracts for Q3-Q4?
Does Treasury/Risk have appetite for a multi-quarter commodity commitment given current volatility?

arguments_for: Procurement can act on forward contracts independently of Sales' pricing execution, allowing parallel workstreams.
arguments_against: Coordinating SKU-level price realization with forward-contract timing across two teams (Sales and Procurement) increases execution complexity and risk of misalignment with opt_1's overlapping non-anchor surcharge.
key_questions: How will opt_3's non-anchor price realization be reconciled with opt_1's non-anchor surcharge to avoid conflicting customer-facing pricing actions on the same accounts?

implementation_triggers: Base oil spot price index showing signs of continued volatility or upward trend
Non-anchor account price realization plan approved by Sales
Forward contract pricing quotes received from at least two suppliers
prerequisites: Procurement capacity/mandate to negotiate Q3-Q4 base-oil forward contracts
SKU-level cost-to-serve data for Synthetic Blend and Conventional Engine Oil non-anchor segments
Risk/Treasury sign-off on forward-contract commodity exposure

impact_estimate.basis: Sized from the Synthetic Blend + Conventional Engine Oil combined decline: non-anchor revenue (~25-35% of these SKUs) repriced 3-5% yields 0.75-1.75pt direct recovery, with a further 2.5-3.5pt attributed to forward-contract COGS stabilization preventing further erosion. This is a segment-level estimate (Engine Oils non-anchor); the high end (5.1pt) is 71% of the single worst segment's 7.14pt decline and should be treated cautiously since roughly two-thirds of the claimed recovery stems from avoiding FUTURE cost increases rather than reversing the already-realized decline.
impact_estimate.scope_label: Non-anchor Synthetic Blend & Conventional Engine Oil segments plus Q3-Q4 base-oil procurement

key_assumptions.assumption: Non-anchor segment represents 25-35% of Synthetic Blend + Conventional Engine Oil revenue.
key_assumptions.provenance: SKU-level revenue-by-account-type report for these two product lines.

key_assumptions.assumption: Base oil forward contracts can be secured at or near current spot levels for Q3-Q4 delivery.
key_assumptions.provenance: Supplier forward-contract quotes obtained during Week 4 procurement outreach.

key_assumptions.assumption: Locking forward base-oil pricing removes the ~1-month lag risk for future periods.
key_assumptions.provenance: Consistent with the confirmed base_oil_cost -> cogs mechanism; validate by comparing COGS volatility pre/post forward-contract execution.

flagged_side_effects: Forward-contracting base oil at current spot levels locks in cost even if prices fall, creating an opportunity-cost risk versus spot-market flexibility.

proposed_option.description: Implement a temporary raw-material surcharge (0.5–1.0% of invoice value) on non-anchor-account lubricant sales and Value-tier products (which show a 6.42-point margin decline), effective immediately. Value-tier products (currently 19.82% margin) lack the premium-product pricing power to absorb cost inflation organically; a surcharge on this segment isolates the margin recovery from high-sensitivity accounts. This mechanism addresses the timing mismatch: it accelerates revenue recognition to match the accelerated COGS flow, reducing the lag-induced margin trough.

impact_estimate.basis: A 0.5–1.0% surcharge on ~60–70% of non-anchor volume (estimated 40–50% of total lubricant revenue, excluding locked contracts) recovers 2.1–3.8 points of the 7.14-point decline. Conservative estimate assumes 50% surcharge adoption and 40% of addressable volume; high estimate assumes 70% adoption and 50% addressable volume. Magnitude is proportional to the Value-tier delta (6.42 points) and the lag-driven timing component of the Synthetic Blend compression.
